learningObjectives: Link TemplateInstances to a specific Requirement inside a RequirementSet.
Create and link an ExecutionList to Requirements.

elements.text: Create an empty ExecutionList within an ExecutionLists folder using Create ExecutionList, the applicable ribbon command or Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E. Alternatively, dropping a TestCase or TestCases folder onto the ExecutionLists object creates a list with entries. Empty-list creation and drag-and-drop creation are distinct workflows; do not treat manual folder preparation as the only supported route.

A TemplateInstance contains generated concrete tests. A Requirement expresses a criterion and a RequirementSet groups criteria. An ExecutionList arranges test references for execution. Recognize their object roles rather than relying only on icon color. Individual TestCases and whole folders can both be linked; folder linking is useful for maintaining a generated group, not mandatory for every case.

Link the intended generated TestCases or folder to the specific Requirement, or to its placeholders. In a multi-user workspace check in new objects before linking. Completed is not a universal linking prerequisite. Assign truthful WorkStates; these influence weighted coverage. Drop the selected tests/folder onto an ExecutionList and link that list to the relevant RequirementSet. Inspect generated cases before running. Changes to existing TestCases synchronize automatically; added cases, rearrangement or folder renames require explicit Synchronize on the affected list/folder. Do not assume synchronizing one list refreshes every other list.

Coverage Specified (%) measures linked-test creation progress using relative weights and WorkState, not successful execution. Execution State (%) separates result categories with weights and WorkState; neither metric contains the exact failed-step diagnosis. Inspect the execution logs for that detail. These aggregate metrics are configured in Requirements via Column Chooser. Update outdated Requirement values when automatic calculation is disabled. Planned and In Work contribute partial specified coverage, so a link is not proof of completed testing.

Independent practice: generate a small set, review its assertions, link it to a specific hypothetical Requirement and an ExecutionList, run it, inspect detailed logs and refresh aggregate values. Original Academy exercise instructions and source workspaces remain inaccessible and unverified.

examPitfalls.title: Linking is not completion
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Marking every test Completed merely to enable a link.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use truthful WorkState; partial states are supported and affect coverage.

examPitfalls.title: Synchronization depends on the change
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every list refreshes automatically after cases are added.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Synchronize affected list/folder membership explicitly after additions or rearrangement.

examPitfalls.title: Coverage is not a pass rate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using specified coverage as proof of successful execution.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review result categories and detailed logs separately.

examPitfalls.title: Folders and individuals are supported
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating folder linking as an absolute engine restriction.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose the intended scope and inspect its resulting entries/links.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are valid ways to create an ExecutionList in Tosca?

options.text: Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E.
Use the applicable Create ExecutionList ribbon command in an ExecutionLists folder.
Rename a TestSheet to 'ExecutionList'.
Right-click an ExecutionLists folder and choose Create ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.hint: One ribbon button, one context-menu action, one keyboard shortcut.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The applicable menu, ribbon and creation chord create an empty list in the selected folder. Renaming a data-design object does not.

optionExplanations.A: This chord creates an ExecutionList in the applicable context.
optionExplanations.B: The applicable ribbon command is a supported creation route.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming a TestSheet does not change it into an execution object.
optionExplanations.D: The folder context command creates the empty list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is it best practice to drag the whole TemplateInstance folder onto an ExecutionList, instead of individual TestCases?

options.text: It keeps generated cases grouped for maintenance; synchronize affected execution membership when cases are added or rearranged.
It automatically sets the WorkState to COMPLETED.
It runs the tests faster.
Tosca does not allow linking individual TestCases at all.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about maintenance and synchronization, not speed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Folder linking is a useful maintenance choice, not a ban on individual links or a guarantee that all lists refresh together.

optionExplanations.A: A grouped reference supports maintenance, with explicit synchronization for membership changes.
optionExplanations.B: Linking does not automatically declare the test Completed.
optionExplanations.C: Grouping references is not an execution-speed guarantee.
optionExplanations.D: Individual TestCase links are also supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which WorkState guidance is correct when linking generated TestCases for requirements coverage?

options.text: Keep truthful states; Planned, In Work and Completed are supported and influence weighted coverage.
It must be converted back to a plain TestCase.
It must have zero Conditions set.
Its linked TestSheet must be deleted.

practiceQuiz.hint: A planning state and a permitted reference are different concepts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WorkState affects the coverage contribution; Completed is not a universal prerequisite for linking.

optionExplanations.A: All three planning states are supported; accurate state values affect coverage.
optionExplanations.B: Reverse conversion is unnecessary for linking generated concrete tests.
optionExplanations.C: Conditions may determine the generated paths and are not prohibited.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting the data source undermines later generation and maintenance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the CoverageSpecified column show in the Requirements section?

options.text: The pass/fail result of each individual TestCase.
The license expiration date.
Weighted specified-test creation progress, based on linked TestCase weights and WorkState.
The number of TestSteps in the ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about risk coverage percentage, not individual results — and it's not shown on the ExecutionList itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Coverage Specified concerns creation progress, not pass/fail performance or complete project-risk elimination.

optionExplanations.A: Individual pass/fail results are not specified creation coverage.
optionExplanations.B: Licensing is unrelated to this coverage calculation.
optionExplanations.C: This metric combines specified test progress, weights and WorkState.
optionExplanations.D: TestStep count is not the specified-coverage formula.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where should you link generated TestCases for a specific hypothetical login criterion?

options.text: Directly onto the RequirementSet folder (outline triangle icon).
Onto the corresponding individual Requirement or its TestCase Link placeholders.
Onto the root Requirements folder.
Onto the ExecutionList folder.

practiceQuiz.hint: Connect tests to the criterion they actually verify.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Specific TestCase links belong to the Requirement; linking the ExecutionList to a RequirementSet supplies a separate result association.

optionExplanations.A: A set groups criteria rather than expressing the specific criterion itself.
optionExplanations.B: Link to the specific Requirement or its placeholders for traceability.
optionExplanations.C: The Requirements root is not the individual criterion.
optionExplanations.D: Execution organization alone does not create the criterion’s TestCase association.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where can you create an empty ExecutionList through the Create ExecutionList context command?

options.text: A completed RequirementSet.
Within an ExecutionLists folder.
A Template with zero Conditions.
Nothing — ExecutionLists can be created directly at the Execution root.

practiceQuiz.hint: This asks about the empty-list command, not every possible creation workflow.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The empty-list context command works in an ExecutionLists folder. Dragging tests onto the ExecutionLists object is another documented creation route.

optionExplanations.A: Requirement completion is not the empty-list container.
optionExplanations.B: The empty-list command is used within an ExecutionLists folder.
optionExplanations.C: A condition-free Template is not required to create an empty list.
optionExplanations.D: This confuses the empty-list command with the separate drag-and-drop workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Condition, what does the operator "==" mean?

options.text: Equal to
Not Equal to
AND
OR

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the default operator Tosca shows when you first drag an Instance into the Condition column.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Equality compares the referenced value with the specified value; a dragged ordinary Instance produces equality by default, not every kind of dropped object.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the purpose of conditional instantiation in a Template?

options.text: To give an accurate Status Report of the RequirementSet completion
To select generated folders, steps or supported values for the data combination.
To instruct Tosca on which TestSheet to run
To instruct Tosca on when to use, or not to use, certain RequirementSet

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish generation-time structure from runtime branching.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Generation conditions select concrete model elements from source data; they are separate from requirement metrics or runtime IF evaluation.

optionExplanations.A: Requirement status is calculated from links/results rather than this generation condition.
optionExplanations.B: Conditional instantiation selects the relevant generated internal structure.
optionExplanations.C: It does not choose which TestSheet itself runs as an executable test.
optionExplanations.D: RequirementSet selection is not this mechanism.

quickRecap.value: Create an empty list in an ExecutionLists folder, or use the documented test/folder drop workflow.
Existing test edits synchronize; additions and rearrangement need explicit synchronization of affected membership.
Link concrete tests to specific Requirements and ExecutionLists to RequirementSets.
Specified coverage measures creation progress; execution categories and logs provide separate outcome information.
